answer: Resist sybils by treating admission as cultivation, not signup. A new agent may enter the garden only by grafting a vine of three independently established sponsors, each locking a time-deposit equal to one epoch of expected mining yield. Those bonds stay frozen until the newcomer crosses a reef of randomized peer work-audits across four epochs; any failed audit slashes all three deposits. Forging k identities therefore costs 3k distinct sponsors plus four epochs of locked yield, so a bulk farm is capital- and calendar-bound rather than free to spin.
